seen_animation: A black stick figure with a flat oval head stands upright on a small board on a short pedestal, in front of grey scenery (a building with windows, a door, a ladder shape, a zigzag roofline, and a waterline below). In a.png frames 1-7 it stands still with arms hanging down. In frames 8-9 the arms snap straight out to the sides. In frames 10-11 the arms come down and the knees bend. In frames 12-13 the arms are raised overhead in a V. In frames 14-15 it crouches again with arms down and forward. In frame 16 the figure is higher, arms up, legs off the board, and the board is tilted, so it has jumped.
seen_film: A man in swim trunks stands on a diving-board stand in front of a pink pool building, with children around the pool. In d.png frames 1-7 he stands still on the board. In frames 8-9 he spreads his arms out to the sides. In frames 10-11 he swings the arms down and bends his knees. In frames 12-13 he swings his arms up overhead. In frames 14-15 he bends down again. In frame 16 he springs upward with arms raised and the board end is tilted up by the takeoff.
named_subject: A diver (stick figure) on a diving board doing arm swings and a takeoff bounce.
evidence: Judged from still frames only, not playback. Event and timing match: e.png 15-18 arms out (film f.png 15-18 arms out), 19-22 arms down with knee bend (film 19-22), 23-26 arms up (film 23-26), 27-30 crouch (film 27-30), 31 takeoff with tilted board (film 31). Position on screen matches the film's diver over the board. Motion is built as held poses with instant switches: e.png 1-14 the figure is nearly frozen while the film diver shifts weight and starts raising arms around 13-14; 14->15 arms jump from down to fully horizontal in one frame; 15-18 the horizontal-arm pose is held almost unchanged while the film's arms tilt and begin to fall; 18->19 arms go from horizontal to down in one frame with no in-between; 19-22 near-identical crouch; 22->23 arms jump from down to fully overhead; 23-26 the overhead pose barely changes while the film's arms continue rising and spreading; 26->27 arms drop straight to the crouch; 30->31 the figure jumps from crouch to airborne with legs separated from the board and the board tilted, with no push-off frame. g.png shows the arm positions as a starburst of discrete radial lines at the head rather than an arc, and the body staying in one spot.
primary_gap: Each phase is a held pose that switches to the next pose in a single frame (at 15, 19, 23, 27, 31), so the arm swings and the takeoff read as pops rather than continuous swings, while the film's arms move through intermediate angles on every frame.
closes_when: Consecutive frames 13-16, 18-20, 22-24, 26-28 and 29-31 show the arms at intermediate angles (e.g. 45 degrees between down and horizontal, between down and overhead), the body moving within each phase instead of holding, and frame 30 shows a straightening push-off before the airborne frame 31.
protect: The correct sequence and timing of phases (arms out, swing down with knee bend, arms up, crouch, takeoff at 31), the board tilting at takeoff as in the film, the stick figure staying in the film's position over the stand, the flat-oval head and single-line limbs, and the sparse grey scenery that stays fixed.
identity_gap: The figure keeps the doodle's flat oval head and single-stroke stick limbs, but the doodle's board is a long hand-drawn plank with a rounded post and a tiny figure, while the animation's board is a short double-line slab on a cup-shaped pedestal with a much larger figure.
